rough.hint: No FSD yet. List the features or epics, mark each as Application, Data platform or AI product, and give it a T-shirt size and complexity. Data platform and AI product features expand into their own drivers using the proxies under Assumptions. Application features expand into screens, fields, APIs, integrations, rules, journeys, batch and file interfaces, events and workflows. Channels and languages apply to the whole scope.

page.readOnly: You are viewing this estimate. Only Estimators and QE Leads of the project can change it.

detailTab.hint: FSD available. Work through the sections in order and open one to edit it. Each header shows what the section currently adds up to. Data platform and AI product sections only count when the change has those requirements.

app.hint: Count each item in the FSD by complexity. The Complexity guide (section 9) explains how to choose Simple, Medium or Complex.
app.roughCmp: Rough said {f} fields, {r} roles, {a} protected actions, {w} approval workflows, {k} critical rules, {v} variants and {l} languages.

fields.hint: Input fields are the fields users enter on screens. API request fields are the unique fields in request DTOs; response and event payload fields are the unique fields the service returns or publishes. Count shared DTOs once. Take them from the FSD or the OpenAPI spec, or leave 0 to estimate.
fields.response: Response and event payload fields, unique (0 = estimate)
fields.apiNote: Estimated if left at 0: {r} request fields and {p} response and payload fields from {a} APIs and {t} topics, after {u} DTO reuse.
fields.byType: Fields by type (optional, from the FSD field list)
fields.byTypeHint: Leave every count at 0 to use Input fields (total) with the typical field mix under Assumptions. Once you enter any count here, these counts replace the total.
fields.lockedNote: Input fields (total) is now locked to {n}, the sum of the counts above. Set every count back to 0 to type a total again.
fields.mixNote: No counts entered, so the model uses Input fields (total), {n}, with the typical field mix: {p} matrix cases per field.

rules.hint: Protected actions are permission-checked actions outside workflows, such as view balance or export; role-gated workflow transitions are added automatically. Critical rules are regulatory or money-moving rules such as AML thresholds, limits, interest and fees. Variants are the products, customer segments or currencies that change a rule's outcome.

data.hint: Fill this section when the change has Data Lake, Data Warehouse or ETL requirements; leave it at 0 otherwise. Counts come from the source-to-target mapping spec, the data model and the data quality catalogue.

ai.hint: Fill this section when the change has chatbot, OCR or AI workflow requirements; leave it at 0 otherwise. AI outputs are not deterministic, so they are sized as labelled evaluation samples, human review per run and analysis, not as pass/fail cases. Golden sets, prompts and OCR samples must be synthetic or anonymised: never real customer data, citizen ID scans or statements.

pt.hint: List the business journeys, APIs, batch jobs and AI calls that must meet performance targets. Performance testing is sized by scripted scenarios, test runs and test-and-tune cycles, not by test cases, and is included in the combined QE total.
pt.scen: Performance scenarios (journeys or APIs under load)
pt.note: Test types apply to rough and detailed mode. Simple: one API. Medium: a short journey or batch job. Complex: a multi-step journey with login, correlation and dynamic data, or an AI call under load.

derived.hint: Calculated from the counts above, the assumptions and the shift-left evidence. Each row matches a driver row in the rough vs detailed comparison.

f.rule: ({k} critical × full table + {s} standard × {std}) × variants {v}× × mutation {m}×
f.fieldTyped: {f} fields by type × {p} matrix cases each × {s} back in SIT
f.fieldMix: {f} fields × {p} matrix cases each (typical mix) × {s} back in SIT
f.fieldBE: ({f} request fields, {src}, × {p} matrix cases + {a} APIs × {o} API-only cases) × {s} back in SIT
f.mapping: {f} response and payload fields, {src}, × {m} × (1 + {fs} format checks) × {s} back in SIT
f.channel: screen and journey cases × {w} (second web stack) + screen cases × ({l} − 1) × {ls}
f.mobile: {n} mobile channel(s): (web journey cases × share + (web screen cases × share + screens × share × mobile-only cases) × (1 + {d} devices)){up} + {r} release cases
f.dataSource: {n} feeds × {c} cases by complexity × {s} (data contract credit)
f.dataModel: {n} tables × {c} cases by complexity + {d} SCD dimensions × {e}
f.dataMapping: {n} mapped columns × {c} checks × {s} back in SIT
f.dataQuality: {n} data quality rules × {c} cases × {s} back in SIT
f.dataPrep: {n} feeds × {h} h × {c} load cycles (hours, no cases)
f.aiIntent: {n} intents × {u} utterances by complexity × {l} languages; label {m} min, review {r} of outputs × {i} runs
f.aiRag: {n} sources × {q} questions × {l} languages; reference answer {m} min
f.aiOcr: {n} document types × {q} samples by complexity; label {m} min each
f.aiEval: {i} evaluation runs × {h} h analysis (hours, no cases)
f.ptDesign: {n} scenarios × {s} h scripting by complexity × (1 − {r} reused) + workload model {w} h + test data {d} h = {h} h
f.ptRun: {n} runs, {r} h per cycle × {c} cycles × (1 + {a} analysis) + {p} h report = {h} h

guide.hint: How to choose Simple, Medium or Complex. Hours per item use the detailed-mode effort settings, before shift-left credits, uplifts and variants.

api.0: Read or basic CRUD, few fields, no downstream call
api.1: Business logic, one downstream call or a state change
api.2: Orchestrates several systems, moves money, or has compensation or rollback paths

screen.0: Display or a simple form with fewer than 10 fields
screen.1: Form with conditional fields, lookups or several actions
screen.2: Multi-step wizard, dynamic sections or complex page state

integration.0: One-way call to a stable system that has a sandbox
integration.1: Request and response with mapping and error codes
integration.2: Asynchronous or two-way, retries, reconciliation, or a core-banking system with test windows

rule.0: One or two conditions, one outcome
rule.1: Three or four conditions, or a tiered value
rule.2: Five or more conditions, several outcomes, or dates and thresholds combined

workflow.1: 4 to 6 transitions with a reject or rework path
workflow.2: 7 or more transitions, parallel approvals, timeouts or escalation

batch.0: One file or job with no dependencies
batch.1: Depends on another job, or has rejects to handle
batch.2: Chain of jobs with cut-off, restart and reconciliation

event.1: Consumer updates state and must ignore duplicates
event.2: Ordering matters, saga or compensation, replay

journey.2: Four or more systems, or money moving end to end

feed.label: Data source or feed
feed.0: One file or table, stable schema
feed.1: Several entities or CDC, occasional schema change
feed.2: Many entities, late or out-of-order data, frequent schema change

pipe.label: ETL / ELT pipeline
pipe.2: Many sources, SCD history, incremental logic and dependencies

table.label: Target table
table.1: Cleansed table with keys and rules
table.2: Curated fact or dimension with history

report.label: Report, mart or dashboard
report.2: Regulatory or financial totals reconciled to source

intent.label: Chatbot intent
intent.1: Several turns or slots, one tool call
intent.2: Multi-step task with tools, authorization and hand-off

ocr.label: OCR document type
ocr.2: Handwriting, stamps, poor scans or many versions

groups.spares: What each L1 test spares SIT

mut.desc: Measures the domain and service unit tests (JUnit 5 + Mockito): do they fail when the logic is wrong?

rule.desc: Share of business rules with decision-table unit tests (limits, fees, eligibility, rate-limit buckets)

be.desc: Jakarta constraints on request DTOs, entities and custom annotations, each with a failing test

map.desc: MapStruct or ModelMapper mappers and @JsonTest: field names, money, dates, enums, nulls, hidden internal fields

jacoco.desc: Shows which code the unit tests ran

fe.desc: Validators and Zod schemas that mirror the backend constraints (field validation matrix)

feunit.desc: Vitest or Jest on pure TypeScript, pipes, signal stores, hooks, reducers and selectors

femut.desc: Checks that the frontend unit tests fail when UI logic is wrong

ios.desc: Coverage of view models, services and validators in the Swift app

android.desc: Coverage of view models, repositories and validators in the Kotlin app

dq.what: Data pipeline tests (dbt tests, Great Expectations)
dq.desc: Share of mapped columns and data quality rules tested in CI

contract.desc: Share of source feeds with schema or contract tests in CI

evalci.desc: The golden set is re-scored on every model, prompt or retrieval change

reuse.desc: Share of AI evaluation samples already labelled in an earlier release

ptci.desc: k6 or Gatling runs per service in Jenkins with latency budgets

apm.desc: Traces, metrics and dashboards already available in the performance environment

ptreuse.desc: Share of scenarios scripted in an earlier release

l4.desc: Cross-system journeys run by QE in SIT

eff.mutOk: Business-rule cases and retest rate stay at base.
eff.mutWeak: Business-rule cases +{u}%, retest rate {w}% instead of {r}%.
eff.creditApi: SIT runs {n} sample case per API.
eff.creditScreen: SIT runs {n} sample case per screen.
eff.creditPartial: {p}% of field cases come back into SIT.
eff.creditFull: SIT repeats the full field-type matrix by hand: about {n} cases per field.
eff.l4On: {n} journey cases in the detailed estimate.
eff.l4Off: Journeys are excluded from SIT sizing.
eff.mapOk: SIT does not re-check field mapping or JSON formats.
eff.mapPartial: {p}% of mapping checks come back into SIT: {n} cases.
eff.mapFull: SIT checks every API response and event payload by hand: {n} cases.
eff.jacoco: Informational, not credited. Coverage shows the code ran; the mutation score shows the tests catch bugs, so only mutation changes the estimate.
eff.feunitWeak: Screen cases +{u}%: UI logic defects reach SIT.
eff.femutWeak: Screen cases +{u}%: weak frontend tests let defects through.
eff.ruleOk: Standard rules: SIT runs {n} wiring case per rule. Critical rules are always tested in full.
eff.rulePartial: {p}% of standard-rule cases come back into SIT. Critical rules are always tested in full.
eff.ruleFull: SIT runs every decision-table case for every rule.
eff.mobileOff: Select the channel in the scope tabs to count it.
eff.ptOff: Mark features as performance-critical or add scenarios to count it.
eff.ptciOn: {c} test and tune cycles instead of {d}.
eff.ptReuseOn: Scripting effort falls by the same share.
eff.ptReuseOff: Every scenario is scripted from scratch.
eff.daOff: Add data platform or AI product drivers in the scope tabs to count it.
eff.dqSample: SIT repeats {s} of column and data quality checks as a sample.
eff.dqPartial: {s} of column and data quality checks come back into SIT.
eff.dqFull: SIT checks every mapped column and data quality rule.
eff.ctSample: SIT runs one check per feed.
eff.ctPartial: {s} of feed cases come back into SIT.
eff.evalci: A person reviews {p} of outputs per evaluation run.
eff.reuseOff: Every sample is labelled from scratch.

r0.test: Domain and service unit tests (JUnit 5 + Mockito)
r0.proves: Method logic, calculations, business rules and error paths of one class, with its collaborators mocked
r0.effect: Below the gate: business-rule cases +25% and retest rate 30% instead of 20%

r1.proves: That the unit tests fail when the code is wrong, which line coverage alone cannot show
r1.measured: Score ≥ 70% overall, 80% in service and domain packages
r1.effect: Drives the business-rule and retest effect above

r2.proves: Every Jakarta constraint on DTOs, entities and custom annotations rejects bad input
r2.effect: Credits backend field cases: one sample per API, half, or all of them

r3.proves: Entity, DTO and JSON stay in step: names, money, dates, enums and nulls map correctly and internal fields stay hidden
r3.measured: Share of mappers and DTOs with tests
r3.effect: Credits about 1.4 checks per response or payload field

r4.test: Business rule unit tests (limits, fees, eligibility, rate-limit buckets)
r4.proves: Every decision-table branch and threshold of a rule, without Spring
r4.measured: Share of rules with decision-table unit tests; PIT checks their strength
r4.effect: Credits standard rules: one wiring case each, half, or the full table. Critical rules always run in full

r5.proves: Which code ran during the tests
r5.effect: Informational only, so the same tests are not credited twice

r6.proves: The UI rejects what the API rejects, field by field
r6.effect: Credits frontend field cases: one sample per screen, half, or all of them

r7.proves: Pure TypeScript logic, pipes, signal stores, hooks, reducers and selectors

r8.test: iOS and Android unit tests (XCTest, JUnit, Espresso)
r8.proves: View models, services, repositories and validators of the native apps
r8.effect: Below the gate: that platform's mobile cases +20%

r9.proves: That the frontend unit tests fail when UI logic is wrong

evidenceTab.footnote: L2 slices, L3 integration and L4 contract tests also shift work left, but this tab credits only L1 evidence. Their effect shows up in fewer defects and a lower retest rate once you calibrate.

teamTab.mixNorm: Mix adds up to {n}%. The model normalises it to 100%.
teamTab.autoOn: {a}% of the regression pass is automated, so manual regression covers {m}% of cases instead of {r}%.
teamTab.autoOff: The regression pass is fully manual.
teamTab.aiOn: {lvl}: test design time −{p}%, including validation design. Use only synthetic data in prompts and generated test data, never real customer data or PII.
teamTab.aiOff: No AI assistance assumed. Turn it on only after a pilot has measured the saving on your own work.
teamTab.calDataOver: Data: {c} load cycles × {d} days = {n} days, longer than the {w}-day SIT window. Plan extra batch runs or a longer window.
teamTab.calDataFits: Data: {c} load cycles × {d} days = {n} days fits the {w}-day SIT window.
teamTab.calAi: AI: the golden set needs about {h} SME labelling hours: {d} working days with {s} SMEs.
teamTab.calAiOver: That is more than half the window ({w} days); start labelling before SIT or add SMEs.
teamTab.calAiFits: It fits in the first half of the window, before evaluation runs start.
teamTab.calPt: Performance: {c} test and tune cycles × {d} days = {n} days in a production-like environment, with fixes between cycles. Book the environment slot early; soak runs often need nights or weekends.
teamTab.calPtOver: This is longer than the SIT window; start performance testing earlier.
teamTab.calNone: No data platform, AI product or performance scope in this estimate, so there is nothing to check.
teamTab.hpf: Hours one FTE can give in the window
teamTab.blend: Blended capacity factor for this mix

trace.title: Worked example: how the current detailed estimate is built
trace.hint: This trace updates as you change inputs. Follow it from scope to FTE to check the arithmetic.
trace.scope: Scope: {a} APIs, {s} screens, {i} integrations, {r} rules, {w} workflows, {b} batch jobs, {e} event topics, {j} journeys on {ch}.
trace.cases: Cases: counted drivers × cases per driver by complexity, plus the derived rows (validation, mapping, roles, mobile, accessibility), after shift-left credit = {n} cases and samples.
trace.appHours: Application hours: each case gets {d} design minutes plus its execution minutes × (cycles {cy} + regression {rg} × (1 − automated {au})) × (1 + retest {rt}) × environment {env}.
trace.data: Data platform: {f} feeds, {p} pipelines, {t} tables, {c} mapped columns and {q} DQ rules over {l} load cycles = {h} h.
trace.ai: AI product: {i} intents, {s} knowledge sources, {o} OCR document types and {g} guardrail categories, {r} evaluation runs = {h} h of QE time, plus {m} h of SME labelling.
trace.pt: Performance testing: {n} scenarios, {r} runs per cycle × {c} cycles = {h} h.
trace.total: All hours, each including {oh} overhead: application + data + AI + performance = {h} h.
trace.capacity: Capacity: one FTE gives {w} weeks × {dw} days × {ph} productive hours = {hpf} h, × blended capacity {bl} for the team mix = {per} h.
trace.fte: FTE: {h} h ÷ {per} h = {f} FTE, shown as a range of {lo} – {hi} (±{b}%).
